ws2_interrupted_install_user_file.answer: NOT 'anything already present'. A file is a 'user file' iff present AND (not in the old manifest OR its hash differs)
ws2_interrupted_install_user_file.condition: for each file in the NEW staged payload (except payload.manifest.sha256 itself): if a file with the same relative path exists in $InstallDir, it is 'ours' ONLY if (a) its relative path is a key in $previousFiles (the OLD installed payload.manifest.sha256, parsed as '<sha256> *<relpath>') AND (b) its current SHA-256 equals the hash recorded for that path; otherwise throw on the FIRST such file: 'Upgrade would overwrite a user file; preserve it elsewhere first: <target>'
ws2_interrupted_install_user_file.decision_location: windows/native-installer/install-core.ps1, lines 385-403 in v306; an inline upgrade-safety block in the main install flow, not a named function (Verify-Payload line 256 checks the NEW payload; Remove-ManifestFiles line 212 removes the OLD payload's files)

ownership_record.installed_manifest: $InstallDir\payload.manifest.sha256; copied as one of the payload files (position in copy order is filesystem enumeration order); an interrupted copy may leave the OLD manifest in place, as here
ownership_record.new_manifest_generated: at build time by windows/native-installer/build-installer.ps1 (Get-ChildItem -Recurse | Sort-Object FullName), embedded in the wizard's payload.zip
ownership_record.state: $InstallDir\install-state.ini, written at step 12; holds UninstallerSHA256 and PathOwned; lines 356-367 refuse with 'Existing installation ownership metadata is incomplete' if the marker exists but the manifest is missing or UninstallerSHA256 is absent

precisions: the check only examines files in the NEW payload (it iterates the staged files); a file on disk not in the new payload is never examined here
it throws at the FIRST mismatch, naming one file; enumeration order is Get-ChildItem filesystem order, so which file is named can vary; the error never lists all mismatches
ws2_interrupted_install_user_file.trap: a product file fails both ways: (a) not in the old manifest (new file, or on-disk manifest from an older payload: here 643 entries from the Nov 3 install, not v303 656 or v305/v306 657); (b) hash differs because the payload changed (sutram-link.exe: installed b6c722e9 matches the NEW package, old manifest expects 84d653fb). The guard cannot distinguish user-modified from payload-changed, and there is no repair/reconcile path, only manual removal
ws2_interrupted_install_user_file.unchanged_in_v306: the guard block is byte-identical to v305 (the v305->v306 diff adds only Copy-StagedFiles and the progress/confirm preferences); the trap is still live in v306
ws2_interrupted_install_user_file.v306_log_point: Copy-StagedFiles logs every 100 files ('Copied <n> of <total> files; last: <rel>'), so a stall at the copy's 132nd file leaves the last log line naming file 100, not 132; the log narrows a stall to a 100-file window and does not name the exact file. The R130 hand-back claim holds only at 100-boundaries. The ownership refusal, by contrast, does name its file (the throw message carries the full target path)
